sections.title: Diagnosis Summary
sections.content:
**Primary Risk: Structuring Risk (Answer Structure + narrative packaging).**

Chandini, your profile on paper is strong for a Software Engineer: 2+ years at TCS on Nutanix Prism DRaaS and Johnson & Johnson–aligned products, concrete impact numbers (~25% fewer UI bugs, ~35% performance gain, 8+ REST integrations), modern stack (React, TypeScript, Redux, testing, CI/CD), and a PGDM in Business Analytics plus an ML project with clear metrics. **The gap is not “whether you did the work”—it is whether you can deliver it in an interview with a tight arc:** situation → decision → trade-off → proof.

Your **Answer Structure score (1.2)** is the structural bottleneck. Even with **Role-Specific Technical at 2.4** (your relative strength), answers may still **sound fragmented** under follow-ups: interviewers hear features and tools before they hear **problem, constraint, your ownership, and measurable outcome**. **Resume & Experience Clarity (1.6)** and **Technical Readiness (1.7)** suggest the resume has substance, but live delivery may not yet **sequence** complexity (API design, state, performance, testing) in a way that feels senior.

**Mapping Rule Insight:**
- You are positioned to clear **technical fact** questions once answers are **framed**.
- Until structuring improves, you risk being read as **junior in communication** despite **mid-level in delivery**.
- Fixing **STAR + one metric + one trade-off per story** first will lift **Behavioural Story (1.75)** and **Resume clarity** together with answer structure.

sections.title: How This Risk Shows Up in Interviews
sections.content:
**Scenario A: Resume Walkthrough**

**Red Flag Prompt:** "Walk me through the Nutanix Prism DRaaS work—what did the user see, what APIs powered it, and what changed because of your UI work?"

**Likely Breakdown:** You may list React, Redux, and "many REST endpoints" without a **single narrative spine**: user job-to-be-done → data flow → what broke before → what you changed → before/after metric (e.g. load time, bug rate, release reliability).

---

**Scenario B: Frontend / System Thinking**

**Red Flag Prompt:** "You said you improved performance by ~35% with lazy loading and modularization—how did you measure that, and what was still slow after your first pass?"

**Likely Breakdown:** With **Technical Readiness 1.7**, you might quote the headline number but struggle to **defend methodology** (what trace or KPI: TTI, bundle size, Lighthouse, custom marks) and **iteration** (second bottleneck you found). That reads as **assertion without inspection**.

---

**Scenario C: Behavioural + Ownership**

**Red Flag Prompt:** "Tell me about a time production or UAT went wrong around your UI or an API integration. What did you do first?"

**Likely Breakdown:** **Behavioural Story 1.75** often shows up as **missing conflict**: who was blocked, what you owned vs escalated, what evidence you used. Without that, the story stays **task-complete** instead of **impact-complete**.

sections.title: Priority Fix Order

steps.title: The 60-Second STAR Skeleton (TCS + projects only)
steps.content: For each top resume bullet (Nutanix DRaaS, J&J/My Concerta, performance, CI/CD, testing), write: **Problem (1 line) → Your scope (1 line) → Action (2 lines, tools only as proof) → Metric (1 line).** No bullet longer than 60 seconds spoken. **Score Target:** Answer Structure 1.2 → 3.5

steps.title: Role-Specific Technical Defense (Frontend + API + quality)
steps.content: Prepare **deep dives**: Redux state boundaries across modules, how you reduced UI bugs (~25%)—what class of bugs, how you caught them (tests, reviews), REST integration patterns (error handling, loading, retries), and CI/CD (Jenkins/GitHub Actions) as **risk reduction**, not tool names. **Score Target:** Role-Specific Technical 2.4 → 4.0, Technical Readiness 1.7 → 3.8

steps.title: Metrics That Survive Cross-Examination
steps.content: For **35% performance** and **25% bug reduction**, define **baseline, measurement window, and caveats** (device, route, release). Same for ML project: **93% precision / 80% recall**—what dataset, what problem, what leakage risks. **Score Target:** Resume & Experience Clarity 1.6 → 3.8

steps.title: Pressure Mocks (Mixed: resume + coding + behaviour)
steps.content: Full rounds with **rapid follow-ups**: "Why Redux here?" "What if API latency doubles?" "What would you cut if scope halved?" **Score Target:** Overall band ≥ 4.0, Behavioural Story 1.75 → 4.0

sections.content: Follow sequence strictly. **Do not** add new projects until every TCS/J&J story passes the 60-second STAR test with one metric and one trade-off.

sections.title: Resume-Anchored Technical Prep
sections.content:
**Highlight 1: Nutanix Prism DRaaS — monitoring UI, 8+ REST endpoints, real-time VDI metrics**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "Draw the data path from user action to what renders on screen. Where does state live, and how do you avoid stale metrics?"
- **Prep Drill:** One diagram: **component tree → Redux slice(s) → API layer → polling/refresh strategy → error/empty states**.

---

**Highlight 2: ~35% performance improvement (lazy loading + modularization)**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "What was the **before** bundle or TTI, what did you lazy-load, and what remained the bottleneck?"
- **Prep Drill:** Name **one** profiling step (DevTools, Lighthouse, or build analyzer) and **one** follow-up optimization after lazy loading.

---

**Highlight 3: ~25% reduction in UI-related bug reports — stability and predictable state**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "What **categories** of bugs disappeared—race conditions, undefined state, bad props? How did tests catch them?"
- **Prep Drill:** Tie to **Jest + RTL** with one example test type (e.g. async user flow, regression on critical path).

---

**Highlight 4: J&J / Vodafone CSM — multilingual site, Redux across modules, GPS/maps**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "How did you split Redux modules and avoid circular dependencies or duplicate sources of truth?"
- **Prep Drill:** **Ownership boundary** per module + **one** integration pain with backend and how you resolved it.

---

**Highlight 5: ML project — mental health & physical activity (93% precision, 80% recall)**

- **Interviewer Probe:** "Why those models? How did you handle class imbalance? What would break your recall number in production?"
- **Prep Drill:** **Problem formulation → features → validation strategy → honest limitation** in 90 seconds.

sections.title: Interview Answer Construction Guidance
sections.content:
**Prompt:** "Tell me about a meaningful technical win from your Nutanix or enterprise dashboard work."

**Baseline Answer (Structuring Risk pattern):**
"I worked on React and TypeScript with Redux and consumed many REST APIs. I improved performance using lazy loading and modularized the code. We also used Jenkins for deployment."

**Fixed Answer (4.0+ quality):**
"Enterprise users needed reliable visibility into DRaaS health; the dashboard had grown heavy and slow to interact with. (Situation) I owned front-end stability and load experience for monitoring views that pulled from multiple services. (Task) I modularized monolithic sections, introduced lazy loading for non-critical routes, and tightened Redux usage so state updates stayed predictable as we integrated 8+ REST endpoints. (Action) UI-related bug reports dropped by about 25% and we measured a large improvement in load/interaction after reducing initial bundle work—around 35% in the metrics we tracked for key views. (Result)"

**Why this works:** Problem → ownership → mechanism → **quantified** outcome, without drowning in tool soup.

sections.title: High-Risk Questions (The Landmines)
sections.content:
"Walk me through your Redux architecture across modules—what is global vs local state, and how do you prevent inconsistency?" **(Risk: Role-Specific Technical 2.4 / Answer Structure 1.2)**

"You integrated 8+ REST APIs—how did you handle errors, retries, and loading states so the UI never lies to the user?" **(Risk: Technical Readiness 1.7)**

"How did you **prove** the 35% performance improvement wasn’t noise? What did you measure, on what build?" **(Risk: Resume & Experience Clarity 1.6)**

"Describe a production or UAT issue caused by a front-end or API contract mismatch. Who did you work with, and what changed in process?" **(Risk: Behavioural Story 1.75)**

"Compare your approach on Nutanix work vs J&J multilingual work—what was different in complexity?" **(Risk: Answer Structure 1.2)**

"Your ML project claims 93% precision—what’s the business cost of false positives vs false negatives here?" **(Risk: Technical Readiness 1.7)**

sections.title: Mock Interview Plan (Mentor-Led)

data.label: Session 1: Resume Arc & STAR Compression
data.objective: Nutanix + J&J stories with strict timeboxing; no digression.

data.label: Session 2: Frontend + API Depth
data.objective: Redux, REST reliability, performance measurement, testing strategy.

data.label: Session 3: Behavioural + Incident / Conflict
data.objective: Ownership under ambiguity; CI/CD and quality; cross-team alignment.

data.label: Session 4: Full Simulation
data.objective: Mixed round: intro → deep resume → one behavioural → one technical follow-through.

sections.content:
**Session 1:** Enforce structure—if the candidate drifts, reset to STAR.

**Session 2:** Push on **how** not **what**: measurement, failure modes, API behaviour.

**Session 3:** Demand **conflict, decision, and evidence** in every story.

**Session 4:** Replicate real pacing and interruption patterns.

sections.title: Expected Outcome
sections.content:
**Target Average Score: 4.5** (from a ~1.29 baseline on the composite diagnostic).

**Measurable Change Expected:**
- Answers open with **context and ownership**, not tool lists.
- **Metrics** (35%, 25%, API count) are tied to **method and timeframe**.
- **Technical follow-ups** get **layered** answers: behaviour under latency, errors, and releases.

**After Persona:** A Software Engineer who sounds as **structured** as the systems she ships—**credible on React, APIs, quality, and delivery in Agile**.

sections.title: How to Use This Plan

candidateSteps.title: Record every mock answer (audio)
candidateSteps.content: Listen for the first 30 seconds: if tools appear before problem/impact, rewrite and repeat.

candidateSteps.title: One-page cheat sheet per project
candidateSteps.content: Nutanix DRaaS, J&J/My Concerta, ML project: STAR + metrics + top 5 probes each.

candidateSteps.title: Re-run failed questions in 24 hours
candidateSteps.content: Same prompt until structure is automatic—structuring is the primary risk.

candidateSteps.title: Gate on Answer Structure first
candidateSteps.content: Do not chase advanced system-design tangents until Session 1 narratives score 4.0+ with your mentor.

mentorSteps.title: Interrupt for structure
mentorSteps.content: If STAR collapses, stop and restart the question—train the habit, not the content.

mentorSteps.title: Stress-test numbers
mentorSteps.content: Ask "how measured?" and "what if that metric is wrong?" on every quantified claim.

mentorSteps.title: Written feedback: one fix per story
mentorSteps.content: After each session: exact rewrite instructions for the weakest 2 answers.

mentorSteps.title: No early sign-off
mentorSteps.content: Readiness only after Session 4 holds at target band under pressure.

sections.content:
**Main Rule:** Structuring risk is fixed by **repetition with constraints**, not by reading more theory.

**Suggested Timeline:**
- Week 1: STAR skeleton for all key bullets
- Week 2: Sessions 1–2
- Week 3: Session 3
- Week 4: Session 4
- Week 5: Buffer if scores lag

**Session Notes Placeholder:** [Insert observed gaps: e.g. timeboxing, metric defense, Redux explanation, incident stories.]
